problem:
$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]
$$

The Wronskian of the vector-valued functions given above is $W({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=${{field-1}}.

examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14066416/assets/b6c879d367709165835c2de7cec94895897be567a9e264222506d4b2a63874e0.png)
Find the Wronskian $W(\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2)$ of the above vector-valued functions.
examples.worked_solution:
The Wronskian $W(\mathbf{x}_1,\mathbf{x}_2)$ of two vector-valued functions 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14066416/assets/ebce3767dfd869aa1ebf4bb03b9eb06a7f41dbb4b927a7699982f35d3a43a562.png)
is defined as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14066416/assets/b07428ffa056ae11d8fef349d666abab80e64bfc1822006f42db42a4b21e596d.png)

Therefore, our Wronskian is

$$
\begin{aligned}W({x}_{1},{x}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}{t}^{3} & {t}^{3}-5 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & ={t}^{3}\cdot 4-({t}^{3}-5)\cdot 2 \\  & =4{t}^{3}-2{t}^{3}+10 \\  & =2{t}^{3}+10.\end{aligned}
$$
